title: Special resolutions are aspherical in trivial replacement categories
statement: Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with functorial factorizations, using the model and Reedy definitions of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Choose a universe large enough for all categories below to be small. Use left/right aspherical functors of [lem-coef-grothendieck-aspherical-base-change]. For $x,y\in\mathcal M$, let $A_x$ have as objects the trivial fibrations $v\to x$ and as morphisms all maps over $x$, and let $B_y$ have as objects the trivial cofibrations $y\to w$ and as morphisms all maps under $y$. Let $P^\bullet:\Delta\to\mathcal M$ be Reedy cofibrant with a natural augmentation $p:P^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}x$ whose components are trivial fibrations. Then the functor $a:\Delta\to A_x$, $[m]\mapsto(p^m:P^m\to x)$, is right aspherical: for every trivial fibration $v\to x$, the nerve of the category of pairs $([m],P^m\to v\text{ over }x)$, with arrows induced by order-preserving maps in $\Delta$, is weakly contractible. Dually, let $Q_\bullet:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal M$ be Reedy fibrant with a natural coaugmentation $i:\operatorname{const}y\to Q_\bullet$ whose components are trivial cofibrations. Then $b:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to B_y$, $[n]\mapsto(i_n:y\to Q_n)$, is left aspherical: for every trivial cofibration $y\to w$, the nerve of the category of pairs $([n],w\to Q_n\text{ under }y)$, with arrows induced by $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, is weakly contractible. Neither $x$ nor $y$ is assumed cofibrant or fibrant.

source.place: Zhen Lin Low, Revisiting function complexes and simplicial localisation (2014), Proposition 3.6, p. 14 (citing Dwyer–Kan, Function complexes in homotopical algebra, Propositions 6.11–6.12). No Stacks tag states this homotopical result.

proof.text: Fix a trivial fibration $q:v\to x$. Define $K_m=\{h:P^m\to v\mid qh=p^m\}$ and, for $\alpha:[k]\to[m]$, define $K(\alpha)(h)=hP(\alpha)$. This lies over $x$ because $p^mP(\alpha)=p^k$. The functor identities follow by composition, so $K:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$ is a simplicial set. The augmentation also gives the stated functor $a:\Delta\to A_x$, since each $p^m$ is a trivial fibration and $P(\alpha)$ is over $x$. All these sets and categories lie in the enlarged universe stipulated in the statement.

source.place: Proposition 3.6, cosimplicial clause; explicit auxiliary simplicial set supplied by the agent

proof.text: For $n\geq0$, a map $\partial\Delta^n\to K$ is the same as a compatible family $h_\alpha:P^k\to v$ over $x$, indexed by proper injections $\alpha:[k]\hookrightarrow[n]$. Indeed, a non-surjective order-preserving map $\theta:[r]\to[n]$ has a unique factorization $\theta=\alpha\sigma$ with $\sigma$ surjective and $\alpha$ a proper injection. A boundary map gives $h_\alpha$ by evaluating at the simplex $\alpha$; conversely the family gives its value at $\theta$ as $h_\alpha P(\sigma)$. Compatibility for inclusions of proper faces and functoriality of $P$ give naturality under every order-preserving map. For instance, after precomposing $\theta$ with $\beta$, factor $\sigma\beta=\gamma\tau$ with $\gamma$ injective and $\tau$ surjective; compatibility identifies $h_{\alpha\gamma}P(\tau)$ with $h_\alpha P(\sigma\beta)$. By the defining colimit for the latching object, these compatible families are exactly maps $\ell:L_nP\to v$ with $q\ell$ equal to the augmentation on $L_nP$. For $n=0$ both the boundary and its latching diagram are empty. Likewise a map $\Delta^n\to K$ is specified by its value $h\in K_n$ on $1_{[n]}$, with value $hP(\theta)$ on $\theta$; thus extending the boundary map means extending $\ell$ to $P^n$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6, cosimplicial clause; agent-written identification of the boundary lifting problem with the latching square

proof.text: Let $j_n:L_nP\to P^n$ be the latching map. Reedy cofibrancy says exactly that $j_n$ is a cofibration: apply the relative latching formula to the map from the initial diagram to $P$. The square with top $\ell:L_nP\to v$, bottom $p^n:P^n\to x$, left $j_n$ and right $q$ commutes by Step 2. The weak factorization system $(C,F\cap W)$ supplies a lift $h:P^n\to v$, since $q$ is a trivial fibration. It satisfies $hj_n=\ell$ and $qh=p^n$, and hence gives the required extension $\Delta^n\to K$. This also works for $n=0$, using the cofibration from the initial object to $P^0$; in particular $K_0$ is nonempty.

source.place: Proposition 3.6, cosimplicial clause; agent-written latching lifting argument

proof.text: Steps 2 and 3 prove the right lifting property of $K\to\Delta^0$ against every $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, including $n=0$. By the boundary characterization in the Kan--Quillen model-structure statement, $K\to\Delta^0$ is a trivial fibration, and therefore is a weak homotopy equivalence. Thus $K$ is weakly contractible. No fibrancy of $v$ or $x$ was needed: it is $q$, not the map from $v$ to a terminal object, that supplies the lifts.

source.place: Proposition 3.6, cosimplicial clause; boundary characterization supplied by lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper

proof.text: Put $F([m])=\operatorname{disc}K_m$, the category with objects $K_m$ and identity arrows only; the operators of $K$ make $F:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a functor. Expand the definition of $\operatorname{Gr}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}F$. An arrow $(m,h)\to(m',h')$ consists of $\alpha:[m]\to[m']$ in $\Delta$ and an arrow $h\to K(\alpha)(h')$ in the discrete category on $K_m$; the latter is precisely the equality $h=h'P(\alpha)$. These are exactly the objects and commuting-triangle arrows of $(a\downarrow q)$. Identities and composition agree because both use composition of $\alpha$ and the same equality. Consequently $\operatorname{Gr}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}F\cong(a\downarrow q)$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6, cosimplicial clause; Definition 1.5; explicit identification of the comma category

proof.text:
The nerve of a discrete category is the constant simplicial set on its objects: a string of composable arrows is a string of identities at a single object. Hence $Z=NF:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ is the bisimplicial set with $Z_{m,r}=K_m$ and identity operators in the second variable, and $\operatorname{diag}Z=K$. Apply the Bousfield--Kan diagonal comparison and the Thomason comparison for $\operatorname{Gr}$ to this same $Z$. They give actual weak homotopy equivalences
$$K\ \xleftarrow{\simeq}\ \mathrm{KB}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(NF)\ \xrightarrow{\simeq}\ N\operatorname{Gr}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}F=N(a\downarrow q).$$
The indexing category $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and all the discrete fibers are small in the chosen universe, as required by both cited statements.

source.place: Lemma 1.4 and Theorem 1.6, applied to the discrete diagram of simplices; agent proof of Proposition 3.6

proof.text: Write $H=\mathrm{KB}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(NF)$. The composite $H\to K\to\Delta^0$ is a weak equivalence, because both maps are; it is also the composite $H\to N(a\downarrow q)\to\Delta^0$, since the maps to a terminal simplicial set are unique. Two-out-of-three now makes $N(a\downarrow q)\to\Delta^0$ a weak equivalence. The definition of right asphericity therefore applies to $a$, since $q:v\to x$ was arbitrary. This proves the entire cosimplicial assertion.

source.place: Definition 1.7 and Proposition 3.6, cosimplicial clause; two-out-of-three written explicitly

proof.text: For the simplicial assertion work in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}}$, with cofibrations the opposites of fibrations, fibrations the opposites of cofibrations, and the same weak equivalences. Reversing each lifting square and each functorial factorization verifies the model axioms. The diagram $P'=Q^{\mathrm{op}}:\Delta\to\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}}$ is Reedy cofibrant: its latching maps are the opposites of the matching maps $Q_n\to M_nQ$, which are fibrations by Reedy fibrancy. The coaugmentation gives $P'\to\operatorname{const}y$ with components $i_n^{\mathrm{op}}$, trivial fibrations in this opposite model category. The category of trivial fibrations over $y$ there is $B_y^{\mathrm{op}}$, including its arrows. Thus Steps 1--7, applied in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}}$, say that $b^{\mathrm{op}}:\Delta\to B_y^{\mathrm{op}}$ is right aspherical. The opposite-functor equivalence in the asphericity statement makes $b:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to B_y$ left aspherical. Its comma category $(w\downarrow b)$ has exactly the objects $([n],w\to Q_n\text{ under }y)$ and the arrows specified in the item. This argument assumes no cofibrancy of $x$ or $y$ and no fibrancy of either.
